title: The dual of a perfect complex
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth, separated of finite type and of pure relative
dimension $d$, with orientation
$\gamma_f=\gamma_{f,\Lambda_Y}:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!\Lambda_Y$
of [sk-def-sf-orientation] (the smooth-purity orientation; the base $Y$
is arbitrary within the setting of [sk-def-sf-orientation]). Put
$\mathbb D_{X/Y}K=\RHom_X(K,Rf^!\Lambda_Y)$ and let
$K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ be perfect over $\Lambda_X$. Then the composite

$$
\theta_{f,K}:\ \mathbb D_{X/Y}K=\RHom_X(K,Rf^!\Lambda_Y)
\xrightarrow{\ \RHom_X(K,\gamma_f^{-1})\ }
\RHom_X\bigl(K,\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K^\vee(d)[2d],
$$

whose second arrow is the canonical twist isomorphism of
[sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange] with $m=d$, $n=2d$, is an isomorphism, natural
in $K$; so $\mathbb D_{X/Y}$ restricts to an anti-equivalence on the perfect
objects, and under $\theta_f$ the biduality $K\to\mathbb D_{X/Y}\mathbb
D_{X/Y}K$ is the coefficient-dual biduality $K\to K^{\vee\vee}$, namely the transpose of coefficient evaluation under the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations](i). The absolute case is $Y=\Spec k$,
$f=a_X$: then $\mathbb D_{X/Y}=\mathbb D_X$, $Rf^!\Lambda=\omega_X$, and we
write $\gamma_X=\gamma_{a_X}$ and $\theta_K=\theta_{a_X,K}:\mathbb
D_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$.

proof.text: Write $H(A,B)=\RHom_X(A,B)$, $\mathbf1=\Lambda_X$, $L=\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$, $\omega=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ and $D=H(-,\omega)$. The orientation [sk-def-sf-orientation] gives $\gamma:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega$. The bifunctor of [sk-def-sf-operations](i) sends $\gamma^{-1}$ to an isomorphism $H(K,\omega)\to H(K,L)$. The displayed special case $m=d,n=2d$ of [sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange] gives $H(K,L)\cong K^\vee\otimes L$. Thus the composite is exactly the specified $\theta_K$.

proof.text: The canonical comparison $c_{K,M}:H(K,\mathbf1)\otimes M\to H(K,M)$ is the transpose of evaluation tensored with $M$, using [sk-def-sf-operations](i). For $M=L$, its inverse is the unit case of [sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange]. For $u:K\to K'$, the two composites from $K'^\vee\otimes M$ to $H(K,M)$ have the same transpose: evaluation after $u$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection makes them equal. Bifunctoriality likewise makes $H(K,\gamma^{-1})$ natural in $K$, so $\theta$ is natural. The defining transpose equation for $c$ says that, under $\theta_K$, evaluation $DK\otimes K\to\omega$ is $K^\vee\otimes L\otimes K\to K^\vee\otimes K\otimes L\xrightarrow{e_K\otimes1}L\xrightarrow{\gamma}\omega$. All symmetries are those of the derived tensor.

source.place: entire proof, with formal evaluation calculations expanded

proof.text: By [prop-sf-dualizable], $K^\vee$ is perfect: the local finite-projective hypothesis follows from the equivalent description in [sk-def-perfect]. The Tate line is locally constant of rank one and invertible by [lem-sf-twist-interchange]. Locally tensor a bounded finite-projective model for $K^\vee$ with this rank-one module and translate its degrees by $2d$; it remains a bounded finite-projective model, with the completed, localized and common-stage meanings of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Hence $K^\vee(d)[2d]$ and $DK$ are perfect. In [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] the negative twist is defined as the coefficient dual of the positive tensor power. Evaluation of a rank-one module and its dual is multiplication after trivializing that line, with inverse sending $1$ to the corresponding basis and dual basis. Thus the opposite Tate lines cancel. The inverse of $L$ is $L^{-1}=\Lambda_X(-d)[-2d]$: opposite Tate lines and opposite shifts cancel. Tensoring by these two objects gives inverse functors.

source.place: entire proof, with formal evaluation calculations expanded

proof.text: Use the dual pair supplied by [sk-def-perfect], with evaluation $e:Q\otimes K\to\mathbf1$ and coevaluation $b:\mathbf1\to K\otimes Q$. Under the adjunction [sk-def-sf-operations](i), the transpose $Q\to H(K,\mathbf1)$ of $e$ has inverse obtained by inserting $b$ and evaluating $H(K,\mathbf1)\otimes K$. Both inverse equations are the two dual-pair triangle identities. Thus $Q$ identifies with $K^\vee$ with its canonical evaluation. Symmetry reverses the pair, giving a dual pair $(K^\vee,K)$. The transpose $j_K:K\to H(K^\vee,\mathbf1)$ of coefficient evaluation has inverse $K^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{b\otimes1}K\otimes K^\vee\otimes K^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mathrm{ev}_{K^\vee}}K$, with the symmetry understood. Its two inverse equations are again those two triangle identities. Therefore the canonical coefficient biduality is an isomorphism.

source.place: entire proof, with formal evaluation calculations expanded

proof.text:
Transport the first variable by $\theta_K$ and the second by $\gamma^{-1}$ to identify $DDK$ with $H(K^\vee\otimes L,L)$. Cancellation defines an isomorphism $q:H(K^\vee\otimes L,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(K^\vee,\mathbf1)$. Explicitly, for every test object $A$, the adjunction of [sk-def-sf-operations](i) identifies its map on Hom sets with
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes K^\vee\otimes L,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes K^\vee,\mathbf1).$$
Send a map on the left to its tensor with $L^{-1}$ and cancel $L\otimes L^{-1}$; the inverse sends $v$ to $v\otimes1_L$. The two composites cancel to identities. Transposing these formulas gives inverse internal-Hom arrows, so the construction concerns internal Hom and not only global sections. These are the canonical opposite-twist maps of [sk-lem-sf-twist-interchange], applicable to the perfect $K^\vee$ by Step 3. Now $\delta_K:K\to DDK$ is the transpose of evaluation $DK\otimes K\to\omega$. Step 2 identifies that evaluation with $e_K\otimes1_L$, followed by $\gamma$. The cancellation sends its transpose to the transpose of $e_K$, namely $j_K$. Thus $q\delta_K=j_K$ and Step 4 proves the asserted biduality identification and invertibility. The symmetry retains the graded signs; the shift $2d$ is even.

source.place: entire proof, with formal evaluation calculations expanded

proof.text: Transposing naturality of evaluation gives $DD(u)\delta_K=\delta_{K'}u$. Thus Steps 3 and 5 supply the contravariant endofunctor $D$ on perfect objects and a natural isomorphism $\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}DD$. This gives the equivalence between the perfect category and its opposite, with $D$ as inverse. More explicitly, the inverse on arrows $v:DK'\to DK$ is $\delta_{K'}^{-1}D(v)\delta_K$; the two inverse equations use the preceding naturality and $D(\delta_K)\delta_{DK}=1_{DK}$. The latter follows by transposing evaluation twice: both transposes are evaluation by the unit–counit triangle identities of [sk-def-sf-operations](i). Finally [sk-def-sf-orientation] and [sk-def-sf-operations] identify $Rf^!\Lambda_Y=\omega_X$ and $D=\mathbb D_X$ when $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $f=a_X$, giving exactly the named absolute maps.

Step 2: c is the transpose of ev tensor 1, and lem-sf-twist-interchange says the interchange arrow is the inverse of c. I recomputed that under theta, evaluation becomes gamma∘(e⊗1)∘sym. Step 4: I checked both inverse equations against the two triangle identities, including for the symmetric pair (K^∨,K). Step 5: tensoring with L^{-1} is well defined independent of the chosen cancellation and is an inverse because tensoring with L is fully faithful. I verified q∘delta_K=j_K, and the shift 2d is even. Step 6: D(delta_K)delta_DK=1 and naturality give the anti-equivalence; the absolute case follows with omega=Ra^!.
